item.title: Passed Comprehensive Examinations
item.description: I successfully defended my comprehensive examinations and have become a Ph.D. candidate! A huge thank you to my committee members: Dr. Dominik Stecuła, Dr. Mike Slater, Dr. Hillary Shulman, and Dr. R. Kelly Garrett. I was able to dive deep into questions about political ideology, epistemology, persuasion, and metacognition. I also survived getting COVID-19 for the first time in the middle of writing my second question.

item.title: Top Paper in Political Communication at NCA
item.description: Excited to share that Rob Bond, Erik Nisbet, R. Kelly Garrett, and I received a Top Paper award from the Political Communication division at NCA! Using an 8-wave panel survey conducted over the course of the 2024 Presidential Election, we found that conservatives were far more likely to defend their misperceptions by disagreeing with experts than either liberals or conservatives, even when controlling for the political slant of the claim and individual’s epistemic beliefs. This work moves misinformation work beyond why people false beliefs to how they defend their beliefs when challenged and holds important implications for the correction of misperceptions.

item.title: Top Paper in Social Cognition at NCA
item.description: I am happy to share that Team Fluency received a Top Paper award from the Social Cognition division at NCA. Our paper investigated how code-mixing in a narrative can impede processing fluency and narrative engagement, resulting in poorer character attitudes and out-group evaluations. Thank you so much to my co-authors - Rachel, Elizabeth, Jorge, and Hillary - for their support during the presentation!

item.title: New Publication
item.description: My newest publication, from the minds of Team Fluency, is out now at Communication Research! We found that including foreign language terms (or code-mixing) in a narrative inhibits processing fluency and narrative engagement, resulting in poorer character attitudes and out-group evaluations. This work reveals the importance of measuring processing fluency as a narrative engagement mechanism and highlights the importance of ensuring individuals become more familiar with foreign languages in order to increase their fluency evaluations. You can read the article here.

item.title: First Publication
item.description: I am excited to share that my first publication is now out! In collaboration with Dr. Hillary Shulman, I investigated how easy or difficult processing experiences can influence subsequent information evaluations. We found that when participants had an easy processing experience, they felt more internally efficacious and were then better able to discern between true or false information. This research offers new insight into how metacognitions, like processing fluency, can impact information evaluation, revealing a potential pathway to fight misperceptions. You can read the article here.

item.title: M.A. Graduation
item.description: I successfully defended my M.A. thesis, “The Seed-of-Truth Effect: The Role of Premise Veracity in Support for False Conclusions.” Thank you to my advisor, Dr. R. Kelly Garrett, and my committee member, Dr. Jason Coronel, for their support!
